 SSS planning national ID linkup to speed record updates
 By Arlie O. Calalo
 November 15, 2026
 9840
 Resize 
 Small 
 Medium 
 Large 
 THE Social Security System (SSS) is working to link its database with the Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) by December to make it easier for its over 40 million members to update their personal information, particularly their email addresses and mobile phone numbers.
 SSS President and CEO Victor Alfonso Limlingan told The Manila Times on Saturday that the planned integration would allow the agency to verify members’ identities through the national ID system and simplify the updating of membership records.
 About 60 percent of people lining up at SSS branches are seeking to update their personal information, making the process one of the agency’s biggest service-delivery concerns, Limlingan said.
 The SSS chief said it is working to address the problem by making identity verification more convenient while maintaining safeguards against unauthorized access and online fraud.
 “Hopefully by December, we’re tying up with the national ID. So, we can verify your identity. And then you can update your emails,” he said, identifying email addresses and mobile phone numbers as two of the most difficult pieces of information to update.

 The state pension fund is also exploring arrangements with its partner banks to facilitate the transfer of updated member information to the SSS database, the top SSS official said.
 Limlingan reiterated that the initiative was part of a broader effort to improve the agency’s digital services, including its website, online portal and mobile application.
 Advertisement 
 He acknowledged that updating member information must be made easier but cautioned against removing security requirements that protect accounts from hacking, identity theft and scams.
 Any system improvement must take into account the needs and vulnerabilities of its entire membership, particularly senior citizens who may be more susceptible to fraudulent messages, Limlingan emphasized.
 The SSS chief executive likewise said the agency was considering managed services and outsourcing some information technology (IT) functions to address difficulties in recruiting qualified IT personnel at government salary levels.
 The planned national ID integration was among the measures being pursued to reduce branch queues and improve access to SSS services, he said.
